conflict: none — did not build, stage, or assemble
choice_reason: 1. B explicitly declines to invent runbook content ('no runbook document is provided in this brief, so this demonstrates the action only'), while A's runbook panel fabricates a specific 4-step incident-response procedure (e.g. 'Page the checkout owner if queue capacity keeps depleting') that is not among the supplied facts — a direct hit against acceptance check 3 (no capability beyond the brief). 2. Both surface every decision-driving Payments/Search value with an explicit target or comparison and correctly gate the destructive rollback behind a confirmation dialog that restates the deploy and error context. 3. B has real functional gaps of its own — Image Processing defaults to a 'fetch failed' status in every captured screenshot so its real supplied metrics are never shown, and clicking 'Open runbook' produces no visible feedback for a sighted reviewer — which keeps this from being a clean win, but B's discipline about not asserting unsupported content outweighs A's slicker but partly fabricated presentation for a role where trust in the guidance is the whole point.
suspected_unblinding: none — no builder name, watermark, or tooling attribution observed anywhere in either packet; the dark-theme/red-banner vs light-theme/sectioned-headings styling difference and the runbook-fabrication-vs-restraint difference are plausible stylistic and judgment differences between two independent builds, not identifying signals.

unsupported_claims.label: A
unsupported_claims.claim: The payments runbook panel (interaction-01) presents a 'Next steps' list of four specific numbered procedural instructions (e.g. 'Weigh rollback of 2026.07.28.3 — requires explicit confirmation', 'Page the checkout owner if queue capacity keeps depleting', 'Adjust worker capacity if the queue is at risk of exhausting') as authoritative runbook documentation. None of this procedural guidance is present in the scenario's supplied facts, which list only permitted actions, not a response procedure. This is an invented policy/capability presented as fact.

findings.label: A
findings.description: The 'Open payments runbook' panel fabricates a specific incident-response procedure not supported by the brief, presented with the same visual authority as the real SLO/deploy facts it also restates.

findings.label: B
findings.description: Image Processing defaults to a 'fetch failed' status (app.js sets imageProcessingFailed: true on load) and stays that way in every screenshot in the packet — desktop, mobile, every interaction and every other state — so the supplied real Image Processing metrics (p95 4.1s vs 5.0s target, 0.2% error vs 0.5% SLO, no active customer impact report) are never actually shown; a reviewer would have to know to click Retry.

findings.label: B
findings.description: Clicking 'Open payments-api runbook' produces no visible UI change for a sighted user — it only fires a screen-reader (aria-live) announcement. interaction-01-open-payments-runbook.png is visually identical to the default view.

findings.label: B
findings.description: The 'Data may be out of date' stale banner and an 'Updated ~2m Xs ago' timestamp appear identically in the default desktop/mobile screenshots and in every other captured state (loading aside), so the packet never shows a clean non-stale baseline to contrast against the dedicated stale-notice state — the two look the same throughout.

findings.label: B
findings.description: The narrow-viewport (390px) state capture shows the timeline window left on 'Last 15 minutes' with 'No events in the last 15 minutes,' apparently carried over from the prior time-range interaction rather than reset to the default 3-hour view, so the responsive check is evidenced with a degraded, less informative timeline than elsewhere in the packet.
